places.name: Żelazowa Wola
places.what: Born west of Warsaw to a French father; the parish record gives 22 February, tradition 1 March.

places.name: Saxon Palace, Warsaw
places.what: The family moved when his father took a post teaching French at the Warsaw Lyceum, which was housed in the palace.

places.name: Szafarnia
places.what: School-holiday guest of the Dziewanowski family, where he first encountered Polish rural folk music.

places.name: Warsaw Conservatory
places.what: Three-year course with Józef Elsner in theory, figured bass and composition; his final report read “musical genius”.

places.name: Krasiński (Czapski) Palace, Warsaw
places.what: Family lodgings in the palace’s south annex on Krakowskie Przedmieście, where he lived until he left Warsaw.

places.name: Berlin
places.what: Visited as a student, hearing Spontini’s operas; a second trip in 1829 included a stay with Prince Radziwiłł.

places.name: National Theatre, Warsaw
places.what: Played the premiere of the work published as Piano Concerto No. 2 at the age of twenty; No. 1 was first performed on 11 October.
places.work: Piano Concerto No. 2 in F minor

places.name: Vienna
places.what: Set out on 2 November; gave two concerts; was stranded in Vienna when the November Uprising broke out.

places.name: Paris
places.what: Arrived 5 October 1831 after the uprising was crushed; never returned to Poland and later took French citizenship.

places.name: 38 Rue de la Chaussée-d’Antin, Paris
places.what: Lived here a few blocks from Liszt; the two performed together on seven occasions, 1833–41.

places.name: Salons Pleyel, 9 rue Cadet, Paris
places.what: First concert in Paris, with Liszt in the audience; Schumann had called him a genius the previous December.

places.name: Carlsbad (Karlovy Vary)
places.country: Kingdom of Bohemia (Habsburg; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Spent time with his parents here. He did not see them again.

places.name: Leipzig (Wieck’s house)
places.what: Met Schumann for the first time, and Mendelssohn; he played his new D♭ Nocturne, which Mendelssohn learnt by ear.

sources.title: John Henken, programme note on Chopin’s Two Nocturnes, Op. 27 — Los Angeles Philharmonic

places.name: Valldemossa, Mallorca
places.what: Winter with George Sand in a cold former monastery; he worked on the Op. 28 Preludes and other pieces.

places.name: 5 rue Tronchet, Paris
places.what: Autumn apartment close to Sand’s rented lodgings on rue Pigalle; moved to the Square d’Orléans in 1842.

places.name: Nohant, Berry
places.what: Summers at Sand’s estate, 1839–46; his most productive summers there were 1839–43, except for 1840.

places.name: Square d’Orléans, Paris
places.what: Moved into adjacent buildings with Sand; his relations with her soured in 1846 over her daughter Solange.

places.name: London
places.what: Left Paris during the 1848 Revolution; played at concerts and receptions in great houses.

places.name: Scotland
places.what: Stayed at Calder House and Johnstone Castle as Jane Stirling’s guest; concerts in Glasgow and Edinburgh.

places.name: Guildhall, London
places.what: His last public concert appearance, a benefit for Polish refugees.

places.name: Hôtel Baudard de Saint-James, Place Vendôme, Paris
places.what: Took an apartment in the Hôtel Baudard de Saint-James in September; Jane Stirling may have helped with the rent.

places.name: Hôtel Baudard de Saint-James, Place Vendôme, Paris
places.what: Died a few minutes before 2 a.m., aged 39; his sister Ludwika appears to have been present.

places.name: La Madeleine, Paris
places.what: Funeral held on 30 October, with Mozart’s Requiem sung; ticket holders only, thousands excluded.

places.name: Père Lachaise Cemetery, Paris
places.what: Buried here after a procession led by Prince Czartoryski; Clésinger sculpted the tomb, which was installed in 1850.

places.name: Holy Cross Church, Warsaw
places.what: His heart, removed by his doctor, was carried to Poland by Ludwika; its urn was immured in 1882.
